propositions: Negative caplog assertions (assert not ...) pass vacuously when zero records arrive, hiding loss of test coverage and remaining undetected across full test runs.
Logger propagation disabled globally or logger level raised by test setup/import poisons downstream caplog assertions in the same process, rendering them void while reporting success.
The void window is test-execution-phase wide (one pytest call) and order-dependent: run order determines which tests experience poisoning, making coverage non-reproducible.
Five negative-assertion tests are vulnerable to becoming void through propagation or level mutations, but positive assertions (assert any/next) fail loudly and announce the problem.

An autouse fixture that snapshots and restores logging.getLogger('rebar').propagate at test boundaries and asserts propagate=True at setup makes void assertions fail at their source rather than silently passing.
